q: Pressure, density and ____ are important quantities in physics and pressure is the basic of hydrostatic and hydrodynamic.
e: Pressure, density, and specific gravity are fundamental physical quantities, with pressure forming the basis of hydrostatics and hydrodynamics.

q: The study of fluids at rest is called ____ and the study of fluids at motion is hydrodynamic.
e: Hydrostatics is the branch of physics that studies fluids at rest, while hydrodynamics studies fluids in motion.

q: The study of fluids at rest is called hydrostatics and the study of fluids at motion is ____.
e: Hydrodynamics is the study of fluids in motion, contrasting with hydrostatics which studies fluids at rest.

q: Pressure is defined as the ____ exerted normally on unit area.
e: Pressure is the physical quantity representing the normal force applied per unit area of a surface.

q: Pressure is defined as the force exerted ____ on unit area.
e: The force in the pressure formula must act perpendicular (normally) to the surface area.

q: In SI units, pressure is measured in '____' (Pa).
e: The SI unit of pressure is the pascal, named after Blaise Pascal.

q: In SI units, pressure is measured in 'pascal' (____).
e: The symbol for the pascal, the SI unit of pressure, is Pa.

q: The force in the pressure formula must be normal (____) to the surface.
e: A normal force acts at a 90-degree angle perpendicular to the surface.

q: Pressure is a ____ quantity.
e: Pressure has magnitude but no specific direction, making it a scalar quantity.

q: From the definition of pressure, it is obtained that pointed nails penetrate the surfaces because for a definite force, the exerted ____ is too small.
e: A smaller contact area results in a higher pressure for the same applied force, allowing penetration.

q: Similarly sharp knives can cut easily than blunt knives because of smaller cutting ____.
e: A sharp knife has a very small cutting edge area, which increases the pressure exerted for a given force.

q: Elephants have four large flat feet so they reduce the ____ and less likely sink into the ground.
e: Large feet increase the contact area, thereby reducing the pressure exerted on the ground.

q: Most obvious is tractors used for ploughing has large tire areas so that they do not sink in the ____ fields.
e: Large tire areas distribute the tractor's weight over a larger surface, reducing pressure and preventing sinking in soft mud.

q: In FPS system, the unit of pressure is ____ (psi).
e: The FPS (Foot-Pound-Second) system uses pounds per square inch as the unit of pressure.

q: In Meteorology, the unit of pressure is ____ (hPa).
e: Meteorologists commonly use the hectopascal to measure atmospheric pressure.

q: Standard Atmospheric Pressure is ____ (1atm).
e: One atmosphere is defined as the standard atmospheric pressure at sea level.

q: $1 \text{ atm} = $ ____ $= 760 \text{ millimetre mercury (760 mm Hg)}$
e: One standard atmosphere is equivalent to 101,300 pascals or 760 mm of mercury.

q: $1 \text{ atm} = 1.013 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa} = $ ____
e: Standard atmospheric pressure can also be expressed as 760 millimetres of mercury.

q: $1 \text{ atm} = 1013 \text{ hPa} = $ ____
e: One atmosphere is equal to 1013 hectopascals, which is also equivalent to 1013 millibars.

q: $1 \text{ hPa} = $ ____ $= 1 \text{ mb}$
e: One hectopascal is equal to 100 pascals and is exactly equivalent to one millibar.
One pascal is a very small unit of pressure, equivalent to approximately 0.000145 psi.
One pound per square inch is equivalent to 6,900 pascals.

q: A person exerts pressure on the floor when standing, sitting and ____.
e: The pressure exerted by a person changes depending on their posture due to the varying contact area with the floor.
